newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline wanes on thin demand amid high stocks.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline wanes on thin demand amid high stocks.

text.p: NWE gasoline was pressured lower on Wednesday by weaker crude prices, thin demand and plentiful stocks, traders said.

A 1,000 tonne barge of Eurograde material traded at $197 fob ARA in early trade, but later on the market appeared to be in stalemate with sellers sticking to offers around the $199/$200 mark while buyers held out for $197.
A 5,000 tonne parcel of regular material was done at $190 fob ARA.
Traders attributed the losses to weakness in crude with May Brent IPE futures five cents off at 1149 GMT, healthy stocks and lack of demand.
"Usually the customers call me and I'm having to call them there simply isn't that much demand," said one trader.
Traders said end-user demand out of Germany appeared to be well-covered in the short-term, while product supplies in ARA remained on the high side.
Further out the market maintained expectations of better prices as the market moved into May.
Swaps remained in contango, with April paper quoted at $199/$200 fob ARA while May paper was assessed at $201/$202.
